deviations: split REQUIRES an output array name (rc 2 without one). The old joined form was indistinguishable from the input - that is TSH-03 itself - and a grep over the whole tree found NO caller of string.* outside this unit's own tests and the review repro scripts, so there is no compatibility to keep. toCharArray, by contrast, keeps the array name OPTIONAL: its newline-joined form is unambiguous for ASCII and $(string.toCharArray abc) still prints one character per line.

OVERRULED BY THE REVIEWER (2026-09-07) AND CHANGED: a negative index or count in the SEARCH family (indexOf, indexOfAny, indexOfAnyUnquoted, lastIndexOf, lastIndexOfAny) is a malformed VALUE — rc 1 + RESULT='' through the shared string._nonNeg guard — not an FPC quirk to reproduce. FPC clamps the window with Copy but still adds the RAW StartIndex to the result, so indexOf 'hello world' o -3 would be 1 and with an explicit ACount can land on -1, indistinguishable from 'not found'. Where FPC genuinely DEFINES the clamping (Copy and Delete, i.e. substring and remove) it is kept unchanged. Red first: 017 2 FAIL, 027 10 FAIL. Tests: 017_IndexOf.sh (test 13 rewritten), 027_LastIndexOf.sh (ten negative cases across all five members plus two pins that substring/remove still clamp), 028_LastIndexOfAny.sh.

indexOfAnyUnquoted scans ACount characters, not ACount-1. FPC computes its limit as StartIndex+ACount-1, one short of IndexOfAny's, so with the default ACount it never examines the LAST character of the string. This is the one place the port deliberately does not reproduce upstream.
lastIndexOfAny clamps the scan position to the last character; FPC indexes Self[AStartIndex+1] with no bounds check, i.e. reads past the end of the string.
chars outside the string is rc 1 + RESULT='' instead of printing the word 'undefined' with rc 0 (FPC's Chars[] has no bounds check at all, and 'undefined' is indistinguishable from data under $( )).

Integer range checks REJECT instead of truncating: FPC's Val takes a decimal literal up to the Int64 range and lets it truncate into the destination type, and a non-decimal literal up to 2^64-1 which it sign-extends. Here a value that does not fit the destination is rc 1; everything that fits answers exactly as FPC does, sign extension included.
toBoolean distinguishes 'false' from 'not convertible' through RESULT: rc 1 + RESULT='false' vs rc 1 + RESULT='' (FPC raises EConvertError for the second).
getHashCode is defined on code points, not bytes (TSH-19 asked for this to be documented); the algorithm itself is FPC's and agrees with it exactly on ASCII.

deviations: The option parser is EIGHT PLAIN SHELL FUNCTIONS (`tca._*`), not kklass members. They take the instance's data array by name, so they cost no dispatch, cannot print into a caller's `$( )` (which is what kk.call_silent existed to prevent), and are directly testable. The public members stay thin. Their answers travel in four module-private globals (__TCA_IDX, __TCA_LONG, __TCA_VAL, __TCA_ERR) rather than in RESULT, which belongs to the member that called them.

FindOptionIndex takes a (short, long) PAIR. FPC's takes one name plus a `var LongOpt` out-parameter and its callers try the short name, then the long one; the port carries the pair through the whole option API, so the composition is inside the member. An EMPTY name means 'not given' and is not searched — FPC passes the impossible character #255 for exactly that purpose in GetOptionValue(S).
GetOptionAtIndex is PUBLIC (protected in FPC): the (short, long) merge above hides which of the two forms matched, so a caller that wants the value at a known index needs the member.

GetNonOptions answers rc 1 + RESULT='' where FPC raises EListError, and leaves the output array untouched (D2). Note the consequence for callers: a command line with a lone `-`, a mid-argv `--` or an unknown option now FAILS instead of counting those as non-options.

GetOptionValues returns its values in FPC's order, which is REVERSE command-line order (the downward scan of TCA-17/R10). Faithful, and surprising enough that both the README and the tests say so; overrule it and the change is two loops.

FPC's CheckOptions reads PAST THE END of a short-option cluster. `O:=O[j]` truncates O to one character while the loop keeps indexing `O[j]` against the ORIGINAL length; `-cv` with the spec `c::v` reaches it without any error being raised. The port keeps the scan string intact and records the consuming option in a separate variable, which is identical to FPC for every input where FPC stays in bounds. This is the one place where the port deliberately does not reproduce upstream.
Location returns the directory WITHOUT a trailing separator (FPC's ExtractFilePath keeps one) and '.' when $0 has no directory part, matching tpath.getDirectoryName and the rest of kcl.
Log writes to stderr. FPC's DoLog is empty and descendants override it; a bash port has to do something, and a log line is a diagnostic, not the program's output.
Run maps a non-zero status from DoRun onto FPC's `except HandleException(Self)`, and the base DoRun TERMINATES (FPC's is empty, which would make the inherited Run spin forever).

The constructor defaults StopOnException=true, ExceptionExitCode=1 and Title='Application'; FPC leaves them False, 0 and ''. These are the port's existing values and are kept deliberately (an unhandled error should stop a script), listed under 'Differences from FPC' in the unit README. No finding asked for them.

GetEnvironmentList uses one process substitution per call (`readarray -t < <(compgen -e)`) because bash cannot enumerate exported names without one. That is one fork per CALL, not per element, and it replaces two forks plus a pipe.

The unit gained the LC_CTYPE=C.UTF-8 self-heal block from kcl/README.md 1.6: it was not there, and CaseSensitiveOptions=false folds case with ${s,,}/${s^^}, which corrupts UTF-8 in the C locale on 5.2 (D6).
`echo` -> `printf` in ShowException and Log. The unit was not one of the six 'printing' units P1 swept, so two echo call sites had survived (X-ECHO).
The FPC report's note that GetOptionAtIndex hard-codes '-' (repro A15) is WRONG: custapp.pp:397 compares with the OptionChar property. The port does the same, and 023 pins it.
